title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page continues the 'Longue Marche' sequel (pp. 650bis-787). Grothendieck is analysing remarkable subgroup schemes of an extension N_rho of a finite (twisted) group scheme D_12^* over a base S_0 by a group L_rho. Underlined letters are group schemes over S_0, and Gamma means sections. The notation fits the study of finite 'elliptic' subgroups in Teichmueller-type fundamental groups. D_12 is the dihedral group of order 12, the normalizer of Z/6 in GL_2(Z). rho suggests the order-3/6 elliptic point. omega is a central involution, presumably -1, and {1,omega}_{S_0} = mu_{S_0}. sigma and tau' = tau sigma are involutive 'reflections'. On D_12^* there are characters to {±1}: epsilon_2, epsilon_3 (and nu_2, which seems to be epsilon_2 written additively). This identification is a hypothesis; the page itself only gives the formal algebra.

Step 1 (end of the computation started on p. 79). Do sigma and tau' normalize G^⇆_{rho,sigma} = D_12^*·G°? Since G° is normal, it suffices to compute the commutators with the lifts u_mu of elements mu of D_12^* (formula (151)). Using u_mu(sigma) = omega^{nu_2} sigma, one gets sigma u_mu sigma^{-1} u_mu^{-1} = omega^{nu_2(mu)}.

Step 2 (Proposition). For a section x of G^⇆, sigma(x) is a section of G^⇆·mu_{S_0}. Its image in Gamma{1,omega} is omega^{nu_2(x)}. Hence sigma(x) lies in G^⇆ iff the image mu(x) lies in D_12^{*''} := ker epsilon_2 (164).

Step 3 (Corollary 1). G^⇆ is normalized neither by sigma nor by tau'. Its index-2 subgroup G''^⇆ = ker(epsilon_2) (165) equals G ∩ sigma(G) = G ∩ tau'(G), and it is normalized by both.

Step 4 (Corollary 2). Likewise N^⇆_rho is not normalized. N°^⇆ := N^⇆ ∩ G''^⇆ (166) is normalized by sigma and tau'. It maps isomorphically by chi_rho onto D_12^{*°} = D' ∩ D'' (167); here D' (from p. 79) is presumably ker epsilon_3.

Step 5 (Corollary 3). N'''_rho := {1,tau'}_{S_0}·N°^⇆ (168) maps isomorphically onto D_12^{*'''} = ker(epsilon_2 epsilon_3) (169). The next page draws the conclusion: N''' is a partial section of the extension N_rho over D'''. It then builds an index-4 'bi-section' N^? and an exact sequence 1 → mu → N^? → D_12^* → 1.

Margins. Grothendieck notes the notational clash N''^⇆ = (N^⇆)° and asks whether Z''^⇆ = (N)°. He proposes to compare with the subgroup diagram (38) on p. 622.

Purpose. To determine how far the finite group D_12^* lifts (splits) inside N_rho, i.e. to find maximal partial sections of the extension. This is a step towards a complete diagram of remarkable subgroups of the normalizer of an elliptic-point stabilizer.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The argument is a straightforward commutator/character computation.

Gap: in Corollary 3, N''' maps isomorphically onto ker(epsilon_2 epsilon_3) only if chi_rho(tau') lies in that kernel but not in D°. This presumably follows from earlier pages (epsilon_2(tau') = epsilon_3(tau') = -1) but is not restated here.
Notational overload, which Grothendieck himself flags in the margin: the double primes and ° are used inconsistently between N'', N°, G'' and the earlier (N^⇆)°.

ideas.what: Commutator of an involution with lifts of a finite group in an extension equals a central sign given by a character (omega^{nu_2}). The normalizer of the 'doubled' subgroup is therefore the kernel of that character.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary group-cohomological computation (obstruction character to normalization)

ideas.what: Construction of maximal partial sections and a 'bi-section' of an extension of a twisted dihedral group D_12^* by L_rho, via kernels of the characters epsilon_2, epsilon_3 and epsilon_2 epsilon_3.
ideas.modern_name: Partial splittings / lifting of finite subgroups in profinite (Teichmueller-type) groups; normalizers of elliptic-point stabilizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related later work on finite subgroups and elliptic-point decomposition groups of pi_1 of M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}: Nakamura, Hoshi-Mochizuki and others (uncertain correspondence)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) treats the Teichmueller tower and anabelian group theory; this sequel is unpublished.

missed.claim: Grothendieck intends a complete diagram of remarkable subgroups of N_rho, modelled on diagram (38) of p. 622. It is announced on this page and the next, but here it is only partially carried out.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would systematize the lifting of the dihedral symmetry group of an elliptic point into the arithmetic fundamental group. That relates to later work on Galois actions at elliptic points of M_{1,1}, but the content here appears routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical, routine computation of normalizers and partial sections inside an extension, as part of a long unpublished calculation. There is no new concept or connection beyond the general programme already known from La Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: The '{+σ 38+}' at the top is most likely a page/folio number ('638') written above the formula, not part of the mathematics.
In Corollary 3 the superscript ⇆ on N''' is struck out. The '(-ς)' reading is doubtful and is probably the crossed-out ⇆ symbol.
The right-hand side of Corollary 3 is N_rho (with a crossed-out superscript), not N_rho^*.
In (169) the left side is N'''_rho (struck ⇆) and the map is chi_rho, as in (167).
In the margin the reading 'NB On a N''⇆_rho = (N⇆_rho)°' is plausible. It is followed by 'il faudrait changer notations', and 'A-t-on Z''⇆_rho = (N_rho)°' is a separate query.
